Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Movies NFA urges Ghana Actors Guild to resolve divisions, avoid fresh court battle Source : Kwame Dadzie 21 November 2026 9:23am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The National Film Authority (NFA) has appealed to the leadership and members of the Ghana Actors Guild (GAG) to resolve their ongoing differences through dialogue, warning that renewed tensions could plunge the association into another legal battle.
In a letter signed by its Executive Secretary, Kafui Danku-Pitcher, the Authority expressed concern that divisions among members and leaders had persisted despite the conclusion of the long-running legal dispute over the Guild’s leadership.
The appeal comes amid renewed disagreements involving some members of the Guild and its President, Van Vicker, over administrative issues, with Oscar Provençal petitioning the High Court over matters concerning the Guild’s administration.
The NFA said it was concerned that the tensions could reopen old wounds and undermine the progress of the association and the wider film industry.
“The court’s decision was meant to bring the matter to a close and give the Guild a clean start,” the letter stated.
It added that the years of litigation had already cost the Guild time, resources, goodwill and opportunities, while depriving members of effective representation, training, welfare support and professional advocacy.
The Authority said a divided Guild could also struggle to benefit from emerging opportunities in the Ghanaian film industry, including the Film Development Fund, the growth of local and digital distribution, and initiatives aimed at taking cinema to communities across the country.
“A divided Guild cannot take full advantage of these opportunities. A united Guild can,” the NFA stated.
The Authority urged the Guild’s leadership and members to respect the court’s decision and allow the outcome of the legal process to bring lasting peace to the association.
It also called on members to rely on the Guild’s constitution and internal procedures as the primary means of resolving disagreements, reserving further legal action as a last resort.
The NFA further encouraged dialogue and reconciliation, urging leaders to reach out to members with opposing views while allowing the leadership to discharge its responsibilities through established accountability mechanisms.
It stressed that the interests of actors and the profession should take precedence over personal or group interests, adding that the Guild existed to serve its members.
The Authority also cautioned members against public exchanges and social media confrontations, which it said could undermine the dignity of the profession and public confidence in the association.
“The Authority stands ready to support the Guild’s efforts at healing and renewal,” the letter said, adding that it was willing to facilitate a reconciliation meeting or mediated dialogue if the Guild requested it and all parties agreed.
The NFA expressed confidence that the Guild could overcome its current difficulties through consensus, mutual respect and a shared commitment to the interests of actors.
“United, you are stronger. Divided, the work you love and the people who depend on you suffer. We urge you to choose unity,” the Authority said.
